A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, 19 figures, equations, and Appendix A. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer experiments on linear regression, classification, and nonlinear regression, including generalization transitions and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, training objectives, task-generation procedures, and inference setup are unchanged. The added task-similarity footnote does not modify the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic regression, classification, and distribution-shift scenarios. Orthogonal tasks are newly discussed through cited work, not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: The Bayesian, ordinary least-squares, and dMMSE comparisons remain unchanged, including Appendix A.4. Hill et al. (2025) is a new citation, not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 14A changes its reported pretraining-task counts from 2, 5, and 8 to 2^2, 2^5, and 2^8, respectively. This corrects the stated settings to match the powers-of-two grid in Section 3.3; unchanged curves do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The noise, dimensionality, depth, context-length, training-dynamics, interpolation, and data-diversity analyses are retained. Figure 14A's task-count correction adds no new analysis or experimental evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the repeated-initialization discussion, second run in Figure 11, and four-set averaging in Section 3.3. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation practices change.

E6.justification: The plotted performance values, phase diagrams, comparative trends, and stated transition thresholds are unchanged. Figure 14A changes task-count labels only; its MSE curves are identical.

T1.justification: The equations, Bayesian derivation, and hypersphere-sampling proposition and proof are unchanged. The new inner-product footnote repeats an explanation already present in v1's discussion.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and concluding claims retain the same scope: task diversity governs specialization-generalization transitions, with supporting classification and nonlinear-regression findings.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an interpretation of Hill et al.'s reported failure on orthogonal tasks: their inner-product similarity to training tasks is zero. This supplies a specific explanation alongside the existing qualification that generalization depends on the type of distribution shift.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page footnote providing a GitHub code link, absent from v1. Appendix A.1's implementation, hardware, training-time, and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hill, Eyre, and Creager (2025), 'Transformers don't in-context learn least squares regression,' and relates its orthogonal-task findings to the paper's task-similarity perspective. The remaining research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds code-access and task-similarity footnotes and a short discussion passage. The section structure and nearly all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 14A's legend is corrected to show powers-of-two task counts. Added text also causes limited layout reflow, including Figure 5 moving upward on page 5; no figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects misleading task-count labels in Figure 14A, provides code-access information, and adds a specific explanation of orthogonal-task failures in Section 4.1. These improve experimental interpretability, reproducibility guidance, and contextualization, while the empirical evidence and theory remain unchanged.
